answer: In an attestation graph, trust propagates along bounded-length random walks. For a sybil set \(S\), low conductance, \(\Phi(S)=\mathrm{cut}(S,\bar S)/\mathrm{vol}(S)\), limits the probability that walks enter from honest nodes; from stationarity, escape probability over \(\ell\) steps is at most \(\ell\Phi(S)\). This sparse external cut bounds the cluster’s aggregate voting weight, so multiplying identities does not multiply influence. Lantern, glacier, and knoll may label nodes, but labels alone confer no trust.
